we have demonstrated that a SIMPLE detector can be operated with the desired sensitivity and that the SIMPLE detector can provide competitive sensitivity in the spinindependent sector of WIMP parameter space, but is not competitive in the spindependent sector.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the SIMPLE experiment is a viable and competitive dark matter search.

a 1 kg SIMPLE experiment could provide a competitive sensitivity for the spinindependent WIMP search, and could provide the best sensitivity to the spin-dependent WIMP search, if the spin-dependent interaction is dominated by the neutron.

a full-scale experiment would provide a unique opportunity to search for dark matter in the low mass range of 1 to 3 GeV, which is currently inaccessible to other techniques, including the direct searches with cryogenic detectors.
